newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Almanij says praised for Gevaert deal.
newsitem.headline: Almanij says praised for Gevaert deal.

text.p: Almanij NV said on Wednesday that last month's deal with Cobepa to share out the assets of a third Belgian holding, Gevaert, had been hailed widely by market players.

Shareholders of the Antwerp-based financial group unanimously approved the 1996 accounts, formally approved of the board's actions in 1996 and renewed the mandate of chairman Jan Huyghebaert for six years.
"The unanimity (of the accounts approval) reflects the fact that the operation with Gevaert was greeted with a lot of enthusiasm," Huyghebaert told reporters after the meeting.
"It's in line with what's expected from company managers -- preparing companies for the next battle," Huyghebaert said.
First contacts with Gevaert had been very positive. "There are no major problems, just a problem of fine-tuning," he said.
He dismissed criticism that Almanij was now becoming an industrial holding and was moving away from core activities. "The combining with Gevaert is not something that falls beyond our lap."
CEO Ferdinand Verdonck said that all of Gevaert's activities had already been done at Almanij as well.
Under the Gevaert deal, Almanij obtained 36.5 billion francs worth of assets, representing half of Gevaert's portfolio.
Huyghebaert ruled out announcements in the near future. "Now we're going to study and implement," he said.
Huyghebaert told the meeting that 1997 would be a very satisfactory year for Almanij, whose group net profit rose to 7.1 billion francs in 1996 from 6.1 billion in 1995.
He declined to give details on the forecast.
Verdonck said Almanij's return on equity had risen to 12.6 in 1996 from 12.3 in 1995. Balance sheet total jumped 17 percent to 114.14 billion francs.
He said Almanij took advantage of the favourable interest rate climate to boost money investments by 20 percent.
Debt rose nearly 25 percent to 49.5 billion francs but Verdonck said this reflected financing of the internal and external growth of Almanij's mortgage and leasing unit Fidisco.
He said Almanij had made provisions of 296 million francs to cover the cost of the introduction of the euro and the adjustments of its systems to the end-of-century millennium bug.
It set aside 309 million francs for exceptional writedowns of goodwill for its Fetrisco and Autolease units.
